analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches, workflow source and build-document excerpts against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. The new scheduler (.github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml:9–38) uses a GitHub-hosted runner, a three-minute timeout, explicit actions:write/contents:read permissions, no checkout and a fixed dev dispatch target. Repository context enters the shell through quoted environment variables; no provider/consumer input or secret logging is evident. API errors stop dispatch under set -e. No supported regression to provider encryption, cache isolation (T-041), serving authorization (T-052/T-053), build qualification (T-054), privileged helpers or payment controls is visible.
The new execution path runs ci-dev.yml as defined on dev, not master. That target source is absent, so integration must verify its workflow_dispatch permissions, secret exposure, runner admission, component selection and artifact/cache behavior before concluding the automatic path preserves A-017/T-054 qualification boundaries. The supplied build.md BASE:493–631 documents branch admission, cache restrictions and credential-free checkouts, but is not implementation proof for dispatched runs.
The unfinished-run check at workflow HEAD:31–37 is non-atomic and reads only 20 runs; it does not prove the no-overlap claim in build.md's added lines 340–356 and changelog HEAD:3. Concurrent manual dispatches or older unfinished runs could escape it. No supplied evidence establishes a security impact, so this is not a finding. Review downstream concurrency/resource limits with the target workflow. Documentation otherwise changes only scheduling descriptions and the update date; surrounding native qualification and release requirements remain unchanged.
